{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMdNDs8AAAABZbZQKw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnXy5zhDCuW8", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnXy5", "number": 29, "title": "Preserve VMD bone curves through glTF conversion, reusable playback and Demo", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `6b7f588ba024122a5a805e5d3eff520f1b9d9d21`, the converter, reusable plugins and Demo support solver-free VPD bone offsets but no VMD motion. Generic linear tracks would lose VMD interpolation, and starting playback from the current VPD-modified transforms could corrupt its baseline.

Implement one complete increment: VMD 0002 solver-free bone translation/rotation through PMX conversion, glTF serialization, reusable Three.js playback and the built Demo.

## Expected outcome

Users can convert a supported BDEF PMX with VMD bone motion, reload the resulting GLB or unpacked glTF, and play, pause, seek, loop and reset it. The reusable runtime evaluates retained VMD curves; ordinary glTF loaders receive an explicitly approximate core-animation fallback. Both use the existing Toon/PBR and Outline paths.

Read all known VMD 0002 sections so later records are not silently ignored. Execute only bone motion in this Issue; retain other records in the reader result and report their omission from playback/conversion explicitly.

VMD morphs, camera/light/shadow and IK/display execution, advanced skinning, morph deformation, append/IK ordering, physics and representative-model fidelity remain mandatory overall work. Existing VPD support remains mandatory and functional. This increment does not complete MMD reproduction.

## Context

- `tools/pmx-to-gltf.ts` has no motion option. `tools/pmx-bdef.ts` already preserves source indices/names, scale, original local rest and inverse binds. `packages/three-mmd-vpd` and `examples/rig.ts` establish pose application and reset conventions.
- [PR #28](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/pull/28) reports passing implementation checks. [Merged-commit CI logs](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/actions/runs/39983775415/job/120517541839) actually report 20 unit/integration tests, eight browser tests, 240 VPD comparisons and existing BDEF/Toon/Outline checks passing; two optional WebGPU cases skipped. These establish existing bounded coverage, not VMD support. Formal review submissions and comment collections were empty.
- [Core glTF animation](https://registry.khronos.org/glTF/specs/2.0/glTF-2.0.html#animations) uses seconds and STEP/LINEAR/CUBICSPLINE; nonlinear time inputs require sampling. General VMD time-remapped Bezier interpolation is therefore not directly equivalent to core CUBICSPLINE.
- [Official historical Three.js](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/r169/examples/jsm/loaders/MMDLoader.js) uses frame/30 timing, destination-key curves, separate translation-axis curves and Bezier-remapped quaternion slerp. Its adjacent-frame hold heuristic is alternative-renderer behavior, not measured original-MMD acceptance. [First-hand interpolation research](https://edvakf.hatenadiary.org/entry/20111016/1318716097) corroborates time-coordinate inversion.
- [MMD Tools’ VMD implementation](https://github.com/MMD-Blender/blender_mmd_tools/blob/e321bd02dd0288a3dc9f1974c06597803c060e11/mmd_tools/core/vmd/__init__.py) supplies layouts through light, self-shadow and visibility/IK records. Its decoding recovery and permissive truncation are not requirements. The inspected mmd-parser source stops after cameras; published-package equivalence was not established.

Use a documented continuous-curve profile for every positive bone-key interval, including adjacent frames, with nearest-key endpoint clamping. Reject duplicate frames within a bound bone track rather than guessing last-wins behavior. Identify these as project policies whose original-MMD equivalence remains unresolved.

Retain the existing correction: the old assumption that glTF mandates near-unit FLOAT skin-weight sums was wrong; §3.7.3.3 says SHOULD. Keep the converter’s justified `1e-6` interoperability policy unchanged. Further evidence-backed corrections must record the old assumption, corrected requirement, primary source and rationale; no human approval or independent AI re-review is required. Corrections must not excuse unfinished implementation or failing acceptance.

## Pre-merge acceptance

The Coordinator owns implementation, testing and PR review.

- [ ] Implement a bounded VMD 0002 binary reader covering bone, morph, camera, light, self-shadow and visibility/IK sections. Document permitted section-boundary EOF versus truncation. Validate counts against remaining bytes before allocation; diagnose malformed headers, partial records, nonfinite values, invalid executed curves/quaternions and unsupported versions. Preserve unexecuted records/raw fields in reader results and report omitted execution with counts. Do not copy permissive truncation recovery.
- [ ] Define fixed-width byte-name handling independently of VPD text names. Retain raw name bytes; bind unambiguous decoded names against retained PMX identity, with explicit track-to-source-index mapping for ambiguity, truncation or undecodable names. Never infer identity from sanitized Three.js names, prefixes or the informational model filename. Test Japanese names, 15-byte boundaries/collisions, duplicate PMX names, invalid mappings, unmatched policy and model-instance isolation.
- [ ] Specify and implement `seconds = frame/30`, destination-key control-point ownership, independent XYZ Bezier time inversion and quaternion slerp. Reflect coordinates once, scale translations once and compose offsets from ORIGINAL rest. Untracked joints return to original rest. Cover first/last/single keys, nonzero initial frames, sorting, duplicate rejection, adjacent frames, quaternion sign equivalence and unsupported numeric ranges without accumulation or partial mutation.
- [ ] Add a minimal runtime-independent draft extension for retained bone curves, with schema, examples and valid/invalid fixtures. Define node references, units, control-point ordering, evaluation, defaults and replacement of corresponding fallback channels so both never drive a joint simultaneously. Use core TRS channels for sampled fallback; keep the extension optional and existing material drafts/PBR fallback independent. No general motion framework or unrelated solver subsystem is needed.
- [ ] Extend converter API/CLI for PMX plus VMD in BDEF mode. Reject unsupported mode/input combinations clearly, including simultaneous VPD/VMD conversion unless composition is explicitly implemented and tested. Produce deterministic GLB and unpacked glTF with zero core-validator errors, retained original binds/rest/identity, resources and attribution. Document fallback sampling limits, guard excessive sampling, and fail clearly when requested accuracy or strictly increasing FLOAT timestamps cannot be represented.
- [ ] Provide reusable loading/binding and playback lifecycle APIs compatible with the lockfile’s Three.js `0.186.1`: update, play/pause, seek, loop, stop/reset and disposal. Seeking must be independent of previous playback history. Define explicit VPD↔VMD ownership handoff; Demo pose application stops motion, and subsequent motion starts from original rest. Refresh skeletons/matrices/bounds for both surfaces and outlines; avoid private Three.js patches.
- [ ] Add two distinct original or lawfully available attributed VMD byte fixtures and exercise both on both existing distinct rigs. Include nonlinear, different-axis curves, parent/child rotation and non-keyframe evaluation. Test direct byte playback and converter GLB/glTF reload. Expected values must come from an independent analytic/scalar oracle, not the production evaluator or emitted fallback samples. On these fixtures, exact-path skinned positions stay within the existing `2e-6` meter bound; declare rotation tolerances before measurement. Measure fallback local translation error ≤`1e-5` meters and orientation error ≤`1e-4` radians at keys and a documented dense off-key grid; report observed maxima without claiming a continuous error proof.
- [ ] Extend the actual built Demo with sample/local VMD loading, binding diagnostics, transport, fractional-time seeking, loop/reset and VPD handoff. Browser coverage checks both motions on both rigs, Toon/PBR surfaces and outlines, pause stability, seek order independence, motion switching, malformed input with unchanged state, recovery and cleanup. Preserve existing VPD/BDEF/rendering acceptance and thresholds; adapt assertions only for intentional new behavior.
- [ ] Use existing tooling: `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_CHANNEL=chromium npm run test:browser`, `npm run check:links` and `git diff --check`, with existing Node/lockfile and documented Chromium setup. Wire new fixtures/schema/numerical/browser cases into these commands. Record actual results, failures, skips, measured maxima, provenance and remaining limits in the validation documentation and PR. Tests merely present do not establish passing execution.

## Optional validation

Measured original-MMD captures of adjacent-frame interpolation and endpoint behavior, or comparison against an identified alternative renderer, would help refine the profile. Keep those evidence categories separate from synthetic conformance. Native WebGPU and lawful representative production assets are useful additional coverage; their absence must not become an invented approval/device gate for this increment.

## Required post-merge verification

None required.

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed MMD/glTF model, VMD animation and
VPD pose reproduction goal. Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance
criteria when primary specifications or measured evidence establish the correction.
Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.
